newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse ends session higher.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse ends session higher.

text.p: The Casablanca bourse closed higher on Tuesday due mainly to the return to the market of institutional investors, including insurance companies, after summer holidays, stockbrokers said.
It was also affected by active trading of blue chips.
The all-share index rose 0.38 percent to close at 406.47 points.
ONA Group, a market blue chip and Morocco's largest private conglomerate, rose two dirhams to close at 410 dirhams.
"There is no rational explanation but Moroccan investors are in love with SNI stock," a Casablanca-based stockbroker said.
SNI has stakes in 40 companies which represent the country's main economic sectors.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the market largest capitalisation, gained seven dirhams to close at 645 dirhams.
Unconfirmed rumours said BCM plans a capital increase through right issues.
The bourse total trading reached 44.7 million dirhams, up from 6.8 million dirhams on Monday. ($1= 8.6 dirhams)
